'''Zachary Thomas LaVine''' ({{IPAc-en|l|ə|ˈ|v|iː|n}} {{respell|lə|VEEN}};<ref>[https://www.nba.com/gamenotes/bulls.pdf Chicago Bulls (27–14) at Memphis Grizzlies (30–15), Game 42, Road Game 21, Monday, Jan. 17, 2022–2:30 PM CT, FedEx Forum (official Bulls game notes).] Retrieved January 17, 2022.</ref> born March 10, 1995)<ref>{{cite web|title=Zachary Thomas LAVINE|website=fiba.basketball|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/olympics/men/2020/player/Zachary-Thomas-Lavine|access-date=July 24, 2021}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was selected in the first round of the [[2014 NBA draft]] with the 13th overall pick by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. A two-time [[Slam Dunk Contest]] champion, he was named an [[NBA All-Star]] with the Chicago Bulls in 2021 and 2022. He also won a gold medal on the [[2020 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2020 U.S. Olympic team]] in Tokyo.

LaVine grew up in the [[Seattle]], [[Washington (state)|Washington]] area, where he was honored as the state's top high school player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. After one season at UCLA, he entered the NBA after being named one of the top freshmen in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12 Conference]]. As a rookie with Minnesota, LaVine won the league's Slam Dunk Contest, and was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]]. In 2016, he became the fourth NBA player to ever win consecutive dunk contests. He was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in 2017, where he played for eight seasons before being traded to Sacramento in 2025.

==Early life==
LaVine was born in the [[Seattle]], Washington, suburb of [[Renton, Washington|Renton]] to athletic parents. His father, Paul, played [[American football]] professionally in the [[United States Football League]] (USFL) and [[National Football League]] (NFL), and his mother, CJ, was a [[softball]] player.<ref name=ucla_bio/><ref>{{cite news|last=Kelley|first=Mason|title=Bothell's Zach LaVine shoots for the top|date=November 30, 2011|newspaper=The Seattle Times|url=http://seattletimes.com/html/highschoolsports/2016900848_mason01.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140525213950/http://seattletimes.com/html/highschoolsports/2016900848_mason01.html|archive-date=May 25, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> Around the age of five, LaVine developed an interest in basketball after watching [[Chicago Bulls]] star [[Michael Jordan]] in the film ''[[Space Jam]]''.<ref name=mays_02272014/> Later, he also became a fan of [[Los Angeles Lakers]] star [[Kobe Bryant]], and modeled his game after his childhood idols.<ref>{{cite news|last=Mizutani|first=Dane|title=Three Questions With Zach LaVine|date=November 28, 2014|work=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/three-questions-zach-lavine|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150104033422/http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/three-questions-zach-lavine|archive-date=January 4, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

LaVine practiced playing in the family backyard, where his father had him repeatedly emulate the NBA's [[Three-Point Shootout]].<ref name=mays_02272014/> He attended [[Bothell High School]] in the Seattle suburb of [[Bothell, Washington|Bothell]].<ref name="ucla_bio">{{cite web |title=Zach LaVine bio |url=https://uclabruins.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/zach-lavine/2799 |access-date=March 3, 2024 |work=UCLABruins.com}}</ref> Playing [[point guard]], he was their primary ball handler. By his junior year, he had grown to {{height|ft=6|in=3}}, and he would practice [[slam dunk|dunking]] for hours in his backyard after his shooting routine would end.<ref name=mays_02272014>{{cite news|last=Mays|first=Robert|title=Swinging on the NBA Draft Yo-Yo|date=February 27, 2014|work=Grantland.com|url=http://grantland.com/features/swinging-on-the-nba-draft-yo-yo/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228075844/http://grantland.com/features/swinging-on-the-nba-draft-yo-yo/|archive-date=February 28, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

As a senior, he averaged 28.5 [[point (basketball)|points]], 3.4 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 2.5 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] per game, and was named the 2013 [[Associated Press]] Washington state player of the year and [[Washington Mr. Basketball]].<ref name=ucla_bio/> He was also recognized nationally as a first-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Allen|first=Percy|title=Nigel Williams-Goss makes Parade All-America team|date=May 22, 2013|newspaper=The Seattle Times|url=http://blogs.seattletimes.com/huskymensbasketball/2013/05/22/nigel-williams-goss-makes-parada-all-america-team/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150713023853/http://blogs.seattletimes.com/huskymensbasketball/2013/05/22/nigel-williams-goss-makes-parada-all-america-team/|archive-date=July 13, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> He played in the [[Ballislife All-American Game]], and won the event's slam dunk contest.<ref name=guardabascio_04302016>{{cite news|last=Guardabascio|first=Mike|title=Lonzo Ball earns MVP honors at Ballislife All-American Game in Long Beach|date=April 30, 2016|newspaper=Long Beach Press–Telegram|url=http://www.presstelegram.com/sports/20160430/lonzo-ball-earns-mvp-honors-at-ballislife-all-american-game-in-long-beach|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160505082146/http://www.presstelegram.com/sports/20160430/lonzo-ball-earns-mvp-honors-at-ballislife-all-american-game-in-long-beach|archive-date=May 5, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], LaVine was listed as the No. 12 shooting guard and the No. 44 player in the nation in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Zach-LaVine-128891|title=Rivals.com|website=sports.yahoo.com}}</ref>

==College career==
On June 20, 2012, LaVine verbally committed to attending the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), and playing for coach [[Ben Howland]] for the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013 season]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Patroclus |date=June 21, 2012 |title=Zach LaVine - UCLA Basketball's First 2013 Commitment |url=https://www.bruinsnation.com/2012/6/21/3106788/zach-lavine-ucla-basketballs-first-2013-commitment |access-date=March 3, 2024 |website=bruinsnation.com |archive-date=March 3, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240303184452/https://www.bruinsnation.com/2012/6/21/3106788/zach-lavine-ucla-basketballs-first-2013-commitment |url-status=dead }}</ref> After Howland was fired nine months later, LaVine considered staying in-state and attending the [[University of Washington]] instead. However, he decided to remain with UCLA and their new coach, [[Steve Alford]]; LaVine had inherited an affection for UCLA from his father, who grew up a fan of [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|Bruins basketball]] while growing up in nearby [[San Bernardino, California]].<ref name=wang_03052014>{{cite news|last=Wang|first=Jack|title=UCLA basketball notes: Zach LaVine shaking off slump in time for Washington homecoming|date=March 5, 2014|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20140305/ucla-basketball-notes-zach-lavine-shaking-off-slump-in-time-for-washington-homecoming|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140308074218/http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20140305/ucla-basketball-notes-zach-lavine-shaking-off-slump-in-time-for-washington-homecoming|archive-date=March 8, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Zach LaVine.JPG|thumb|upright|LaVine shooting against [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] in 2014]]
After a strong start to [[2013–14 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2013–14]] as the team's [[sixth man]], featuring an impressive display of outside shooting and explosive dunks, the former point guard LaVine evoked memories of former Bruin [[Russell Westbrook]]'s UCLA beginnings.<ref name=mays_02272014/> [[NBA draft]] pundits began ranking LaVine high on their projections for the [[2014 NBA draft]] if he [[Eligibility for the NBA draft|declared himself eligible]].<ref name=mays_02272014/><ref>{{cite web |title=UCLA's Zach LaVine is dunking his way to the NBA |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/college-basketball/news/20131220/ucla-zach-lavine-nba-steve-alford-dunk/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131221095248/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/college-basketball/news/20131220/ucla-zach-lavine-nba-steve-alford-dunk/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 21, 2013 |website=Sportsillustrated.cnn.com|date=December 20, 2013|last=Johnson|first=Chris}}</ref> [[ESPN.com]] draft expert [[Chad Ford]] attributed LaVine's appeal to the Westbrook comparisons. ==Professional career==
===Minnesota Timberwolves (2014–2017)===
LaVine was selected by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] with the 13th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]]. He signed his rookie-scale contract with the team on July 8, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 8, 2014 |title=Timberwolves Sign First-Round Pick Zach LaVine |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-first-round-pick-zach-lavine |access-date=November 21, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Over the first five games of the [[2014–15 Minnesota Timberwolves season|2014–15 season]], LaVine played a total of 12 minutes. When an ankle injury sidelined starter [[Ricky Rubio]] indefinitely, LaVine became the starting point guard over veteran [[Mo Williams]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Zgoda|first=Jerry|title=Wolves place trust in LaVine|date=November 10, 2014|newspaper=Star Tribune|url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/282093061.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141113192816/http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/282093061.html|archive-date=November 13, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Harper|first=Zach|title=Zach LaVine approaches surprise point guard role with confidence|date=November 12, 2014|work=CBS Sports|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/24800677/zach-lavine-approaches-surprise-point-guard-role-with-confidence|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141113185108/http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/24800677/zach-lavine-approaches-surprise-point-guard-role-with-confidence|archive-date=November 13, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> LaVine moved back into the starting lineup after back spasms sidelined Williams, who had become the starting guard again.<ref>{{cite news|last=Zgoda|first=Jerry|title=Williams out, Muhammad intends to play vs. Warriors|date=December 8, 2014|newspaper=The Star Tribune|url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/blogs/285119951.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141209064422/http://www.startribune.com/sports/blogs/285119951.html|archive-date=December 9, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> On December 6 against the [[San Antonio Spurs]], LaVine had 22 points and 10 assists for his first [[double-double]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Youngblood|first=Kent|title=Spurs handle Wolves smoothly|date=December 6, 2014|newspaper=The Star Tribune|url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/284995461.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141207213044/http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/284995461.html|archive-date=December 7, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

Rubio returned in February 2015, resulting in a dip in playing time for LaVine. However, Williams was also traded that month which opened up more opportunities.<ref>{{cite news|last=Greder|first=Andy|title=Timberwolves' Zach LaVine recognizes ins, outs of playing time|date=February 28, 2015|newspaper=Pioneer starting in 40, and averaged 10.1 points, 2.8 rebounds and 3.6 assists, while shooting 42.2 percent overall and 34.1 percent on three-pointers. He was subsequently named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Youngblood|first=Kent|title=Wiggins, LaVine win NBA rookie team honors|date=May 18, 2015|newspaper=The Star Tribune|url=http://www.startribune.com/wiggins-lavine-win-nba-rookie-team-honors/304146461/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150521001145/http://www.startribune.com/wiggins-lavine-win-nba-rookie-team-honors/304146461/|archive-date=May 21, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>[[File:Kyrie Irving (24009454364).jpg|thumb|left|LaVine (middle) defending against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in 2016]]
On October 21, 2015, the Timberwolves exercised their third-year team option on LaVine's rookie-scale contract, extending the contract through the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web |date=October 21, 2015 |title=Timberwolves Exercise Team Options on Five Players |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-exercise-team-options-five-players |access-date=March 3, 2024 |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref> With Ricky Rubio sidelined in early November, LaVine took over the starting point guard role and took advantage of the increased minutes. On November 13, he scored a season-high 26 points in a loss to the Indiana Pacers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151113/MININD/gameinfo.html|title=George scores 29, Pacers beat Wolves for 6th win in 7 games|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=November 13, 2015|access-date=November 13, 2015}}</ref> He later topped that mark on December 13, scoring 28 points in a loss to the Phoenix Suns.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151213/MINPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Knight's 25 points lead Suns over Timberwolves 108-101|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=December 13, 2015|access-date=January 28, 2016}}</ref> During the [[2016 NBA All-Star Weekend|2016 All-Star Weekend]], LaVine scored 30 points for Team USA in the Rising Stars Challenge to capture MVP honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/14769510 |title=Zach LaVine highlights Rising Stars with 30 points, 7 boards|publisher=ESPN|date=February 12, 2016|access-date=February 12, 2016}}</ref> He also became the fourth player ever to win consecutive Slam Dunk Contests.{{efn|He joined Jordan, [[Jason Richardson]], and [[Nate Robinson]].<ref name=espn_02142016>{{cite news|title=Zach LaVine wins slam dunk contest in battle with Aaron Gordon|date=February 14, 2016|website=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/14774906 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160214184349/http://espn.go.com/nba/story/_/id/14774906/zach-lavine-minnesota-timberwolves-edges-orlando-magic-aaron-gordon-slam-dunk-contest|archive-date=February 14, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>}} The final round of the contest, which featured two tie-breakers with [[Aaron Gordon]], drew comparisons to the contest between [[Michael Jordan]] and [[Dominique Wilkins]] in 1988.<ref name=espn_02142016/>

On October 24, 2016, the Timberwolves exercised their fourth-year team option on LaVine's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite web |date=October 24, 2016 |title=Timberwolves Exercise Team Options on Four Players |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-exercise-team-options-four-players |access-date=March 3, 2024 |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref> On November 9, he tied his then career high with 37 points in a 123–107 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899559|title=Timberwolves thump Magic to earn first road win|work=ESPN.com|date=November 9, 2016|access-date=November 10, 2016}}</ref> On December 23, he scored a then-career-high 40 points and tied a career best with seven three-pointers in a 109–105 loss against the [[Sacramento Kings]]. On February 4, 2017, LaVine was ruled out for the rest of the season after an MRI revealed he had a torn ACL in his left knee.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/zach-lavine-injury-update-02-04-2017|title=ZACH LAVINE INJURY UPDATE|work=NBA.com|date=February 4, 2017|access-date=February 4, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Youngblood|first=Kent|url=http://www.startribune.com/wolves-zach-lavine-out-for-season-with-acl-tear-in-left-knee/412790093/|title=Wolves Zach LaVine out for season with ACL tear in left knee|work=StarTribune.com|date=February 4, 2017|access-date=February 4, 2017|archive-date=February 5, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170205032639/http://www.startribune.com/wolves-zach-lavine-out-for-season-with-acl-tear-in-left-knee/412790093/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Ten days later, he underwent successful surgery to reconstruct the knee.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/zach-lavine-surgery-update-0/|title=ZACH LAVINE SURGERY UPDATE|work=NBA.com|date=February 14, 2017|access-date=February 18, 2017}}</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2017–2025)===
====2017–2020: First seasons in Chicago and breakthrough====
On June 22, 2017, LaVine was traded, along with [[Kris Dunn]] and the rights to [[Lauri Markkanen]] (the 7th pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]]), to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for [[Jimmy Butler]] and the rights to [[Justin Patton]] (the 16th pick in the 2017 NBA draft).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-acquire-dunn-lavine-and-markkanen-minneosta|title=BULLS ACQUIRE DUNN, LAVINE AND MARKKANEN FROM MINNEOSTA|work=NBA.com|date=June 22, 2017|access-date=June 22, 2017}}</ref>

On January 13, 2018, in his first game in 11 months, LaVine scored 14 points in the Bulls' 107–105 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975378|title=Bulls top Pistons 107-105 in Zach LaVine's return|work=ESPN.com|date=January 13, 2018|access-date=January 14, 2018}}</ref> On February 9, he scored a season-high 35 points in a 114–113 win over his former team the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975568|title=LaVine scores 35, Bulls beat Butler, Timberwolves 114-113|work=ESPN.com|date=February 9, 2018|access-date=February 10, 2018}}</ref>

On July 6, 2018, the [[restricted free agent]] LaVine received a four-year, $80 million offer sheet from the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/07/06/report-zach-lavine-signs-four-year-offer-sheet-sacramento-kings|title=Reports: Bulls to match Kings' offer sheet for Zach LaVine|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=July 6, 2018}}</ref> Two days later, the Bulls exercised their right of first refusal and matched the offer sheet extended to LaVine by the Kings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-retain-lavine|title=Bulls retain LaVine|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2018|access-date=July 8, 2018}}</ref> LaVine scored at least 30 points in each of the Bulls' first three games of the season, becoming the third Chicago player to do so, joining [[Michael Jordan]] (1986) and [[Bob Love]] (1971).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070725|title=Jordan gets another double-double as Mavs top Bulls 115-109|work=ESPN.com|date=October 22, 2018|access-date=October 22, 2018}}</ref> On October 24, he made two free throws with 0.5 seconds left to lift the Bulls to a 112–110 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. He finished with 32 points for his fourth straight 30-point game to start the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070737|title=Zach LaVine lifts Bulls past Hornets with 2 late free throws|work=ESPN.com|date=October 24, 2018|access-date=October 24, 2018}}</ref> On November 5, he scored a then-career-high 41 points, including the game-winning free throw with 0.2 seconds left, as the Bulls beat the [[New York Knicks]] 116–115 in double overtime.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070824|title=LaVine scores career-high 41 points in double OT win|work=ESPN.com|date=November 5, 2018|access-date=November 5, 2018}}</ref> On November 10, he scored 24 points in a 99–98 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], thus scoring 20 or more points in each of Chicago's 13 games to begin the season and in a career-high 14 straight overall, dating to his final game of 2017–18. The last Bulls player to score 20-plus points in 14 consecutive games was Jimmy Butler, who did it 15 straight times in 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070859|title=LaVine, Archidiacono help Bulls edge Cavs 99-98|work=ESPN.com|date=November 10, 2018|access-date=November 10, 2018}}</ref> He scored 26 points against the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on November 12 for 15 straight, before a 10-point game on November 14 against the [[Boston Celtics]] ended the streak.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/lavinza01/gamelog/2019/|title=Zach LaVine 2018-19 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 21, 2018}}</ref> On December 26, after missing five games with a sprained left ankle, LaVine had 28 points in 26 minutes off the bench in a 119–94 loss to the Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071183|title=Rose returns to Chicago, leads T-Wolves over Bulls 119-94|work=ESPN.com|date=December 26, 2018|access-date=December 27, 2018}}</ref>

On February 23, 2019, he scored a then-career-high 42 points in a 126–116 win over the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071562|title=LaVine scores career-high 42 as Bulls top Celtics 126-116|work=ESPN.com|date=February 23, 2019|access-date=February 24, 2019}}</ref> On March 1, he scored 47 points in a 168–161 quadruple-overtime win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]], the third-highest-scoring game in NBA history.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 1, 2019 |title=Bulls fend off Trae Young's historic night in NBA's third-highest-scoring game |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071601 |access-date=March 2, 2019 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref> On March 6, he scored 39 points and hit the go-ahead layup in the closing seconds to lift the Bulls to a 108–107 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071643|title=LaVine scores 39, Bulls beat 76ers 108-107|work=ESPN.com|date=March 6, 2019|access-date=March 7, 2019}}</ref> LaVine missed the end of the season with right leg injuries.<ref>{{cite web |date=April 6, 2019 |title=Embiid, Redick lead way as 76ers beat Bulls 116-96 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071867 |access-date=April 7, 2019 |work=ESPN.com |quote=G Zach LaVine (right knee tendinitis, bruised right thigh) indicated he will not play again this season, though the Bulls have not officially shut him down.}}</ref> He led the Bulls in points scored in the season with 1,492 points while playing in only 63 games.

In the second game of the 2019–20 season, LaVine scored 37 points in a 110–102 win against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. On November 16, 2019, Lavine scored 36 points in a loss to the Brooklyn Nets. On November 23, LaVine scored a then-career-high 49 points, with 13 three-point field goals, including the game-winning three-pointer to defeat the [[Charlotte Hornets]] 116–115.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28149806 |title=Bulls' Zach LaVine has 49, hits winner game after benching|work=ESPN.com|access-date=November 23, 2019|others=Contributed by The Associated Press|date=November 23, 2019}}</ref> On November 27, he had 36 points against [[Golden State Warriors|Golden State]]. On January 25, 2020, LaVine recorded 44 points, ten rebounds and eight assists in a 118–106 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/bulls/ct-chicago-bulls-cavaliers-20200126-34hldipiybh7dl2mfkvqrw6sue-story.html|title=3 takeaways from the Bulls' 118-106 win over the Cavaliers, including Zach LaVine scoring 44 points and just missing his 1st career triple-double|first=Jamal|last=Collier|website=Chicagotribune.com|date=January 26, 2020 |access-date=November 21, 2021}}</ref> On February 11, he scored 41 points on 15-of-21 shooting, including 8 three-pointers, to go with nine rebounds, in a 126–114 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Zach LaVine dazzles with fifth 40-point game this season as Bulls fall to Wizards |url=https://www.nba.com/amp/bulls/features/zach-lavine-dazzles-fifth-40-point-game-season-bulls-fall-wizards |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200216185401/https://www.nba.com/amp/bulls/features/zach-lavine-dazzles-fifth-40-point-game-season-bulls-fall-wizards |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 16, 2020 |website=Nba.com}}</ref> On February 25, 2020, LaVine again scored 41 points in a 124–122 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/video/clip/_/id/28782998 |title=Lavine erupts for 41 points in narrow loss to Thunder - ESPN Video |access-date=February 28, 2020 |archive-date=February 28, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200228000146/https://www.espn.com/video/clip/_/id/28782998 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was the leading scorer in 42 of the 65 games played in the shortened season.

====2020–2025: First All-Star selections and playoff appearance====
On February 10, LaVine scored a season-high 46 points with nine 3-pointers in a 129–116 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans.<ref>{{cite web |title=LaVine, White Combine For 76 Points, 17 3-Pointers |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000385 |publisher=NBA |access-date=March 5, 2021}}</ref> With a new head coach in [[Billy Donovan]] and averaging career highs in scoring and shooting efficiency, on February 24, 2021, he was named a reserve for the [[2021 NBA All-Star Game]]. It was his first All-Star selection and the first Bulls player selected since Jimmy Butler in [[2017 NBA All-Star Game|2017]].<ref>{{cite news|first1=Jamal|last1=Collier|first2=Deantae|last2=Prince|title=Zach LaVine selected as reserve for 2021 All-Star Game in Atlanta, becoming first Chicago Bulls player to appear in the showcase since Jimmy Butler|date=February 23, 2021|newspaper=Chicago Tribune|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/bulls/ct-chicago-bulls-zach-lavine-all-star-reserves-2021-20210224-syj5qpqmrfgkjoggj54giil4gq-story.html|access-date=February 24, 2021}}</ref> In the 34th game of the season, LaVine had his 17th game scoring 30 points or more.<ref>{{cite web |last=Martell |first=Brett |title=LaVine, Bulls take down Williamson, Pelicans |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000548 |website=APNews.com |access-date=6 March 2021}}</ref> On March 7, he played 28 minutes and scored 13 points during the [[2021 NBA All-Star Game|All-Star game]].<ref>{{cite web |date=March 8, 2021 |title=Giannis, Curry lead Team LeBron to All-Star Game win |url=https://www.nba.com/game/lbn-vs-drt-0032000001/box-score |access-date=March 3, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On April 9, LaVine scored 39 of his then-career-high 50 points in the first half in a 120–108 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Henry |first=George |date=April 10, 2021 |title=Hawks overcome LaVine's historic 39-point 1st half |url=https://www.nba.com/game/chi-vs-atl-0022000791 |access-date=March 3, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> For the season, he averaged a career-high 27.4 points per game, which ranked seventh in the NBA. He also reached career highs in rebounds (5.0), assists (4.9), 3-point shooting (41.9%), overall field goal percentage (50.7%) and free throw percentage (84.9%).<ref>{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Sam |author-link=Sam Smith (sportswriter) |date=May 17, 2021 |title=Zach LaVine sees brighter days ahead: "I love it here in Chicago... I'm very excited for the future." |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/features/zach-lavine-sees-brighter-days-ahead-i-love-it-here-chicago-im-very-excited-future |access-date=May 18, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On November 19, 2021, LaVine scored a season-high 36 points in a 114–108 road victory over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Chicago Bulls hold off the Denver Nuggets 114-108 behind Zach LaVine's 36 points, finishing 3-2 on a tough West Coast trip|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/bulls/ct-chicago-bulls-denver-nuggets-20211120-ckdw6ilndvgyroipag73klrey4-story.html|website=chicagotribune.com|date=November 20, 2021 }}</ref> On February 3, he was named a reserve for the [[2022 NBA All-Star Game]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 NBA All-Star reserves revealed! |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2022-all-star-reserves-announced |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/features/zach-lavine-ready-take-big-stage-vs-bucks-its-about-time |access-date=March 3, 2024 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Bulls were playoff-eligible for the first time 2022}}</ref> On May 24, LaVine underwent left knee surgery.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 24, 2022 |title=Zach LaVine Injury Update |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/zach-lavine-injury-update-1 |newspaper=AP News}}</ref>

On December 4, 2022, LaVine recorded 41 points, eight rebounds and four steals in a 110–101 loss against the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468505|title=Monk, Sabonis, Kings overcome LaVine's 41 points, beat Bulls|website=ESPN.com|date=December 4, 2022|access-date=December 4, 2022}}</ref> On December 30, LaVine scored a season-high 43 points on 15-of-20 shooting from the field, along with six assists, in a 132–118 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468687|title=LaVine scores season-high 43 as Bulls beat Pistons 132-118|website=ESPN.com|date=December 30, 2022|access-date=December 31, 2022}}</ref> On January 6, 2023, LaVine scored 41 points on 14-of-19 shooting from the field and 11 of 13 from beyond the three-point line in a 126–112 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/bulls-zach-lavine-torching-sixers-mind-blowing-11-triples|title=Bulls star Zach LaVine sounds off on torching Sixers with mind-blowing 11 triples|website=ClutchPoints|last=Songco|first=Paolo|date=January 6, 2023|access-date=January 6, 2023}}</ref> That was his fourth career game with at least 40 points on 70% shooting, breaking a tie with [[Scottie Pippen]] for the second most in Bulls history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/bulls-news-michael-jordan-next-on-zach-lavine-list-after-breaking-scottie-pippen-record|title=Michael Jordan next on Zach LaVine's list after breaking Scottie Pippen record with Bulls|website=ClutchPoints|last=Guinhawa |first=Angelo|date=January 7, 2023|access-date=January 8, 2023}}</ref> On March 17, LaVine put up 39 points, while [[DeMar DeRozan]] put up 49 points, in a 139–131 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. Their 88 combined points surpassed Michael Jordan and [[Horace Grant]]'s previous record of 85, to become the most points scored in a game by a duo in Bulls history.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://clutchpoints.com/bulls-news-demar-derozan-zach-lavine-combine-chicago-history-not-even-michael-jordan-matched|title= DeMar DeRozan, Zach LaVine combine for Bulls history not even Michael Jordan matched|website=ClutchPoints|last=Guinhawa|first=Angelo|date=March 17, 2023|access-date=March 17, 2023}}</ref>

On October 28, 2023, LaVine put up a career-high 51 points in a 118–102 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/bulls-news-zach-lavine-dropping-51-points-pistons-fans-going-bonkers|title=Bulls' Zach LaVine dropping 51 points vs. Pistons has fans going bonkers|website=ClutchPoints|last=Villas|first=Rexwell|date=October 28, 2023|access-date=October 28, 2023}}</ref> In February 2024, the [[Chicago Bulls]] announced that LaVine would undergo season-ending surgery on his right foot as a next step in his recovery process.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-03 |title=Bulls' Zach LaVine to have season-ending foot surgery ahead of trade deadline |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nba/bulls-zach-lavine-to-have-season-ending-foot-surgery-ahead-of-trade-deadline |access-date=2024-03-01 |work=FOX Sports}}</ref>

On November 29, 2024, LaVine put up 29 points in a 138–129 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]]. He also achieved 1,051 three-pointers made as a Bull, surpassing [[Kirk Hinrich]] as the all-time leader in three-pointers made in Bulls franchise history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/bulls-news-zach-lavine-sets-impressive-franchise-record-vs-celtics|title=Bulls' Zach LaVine sets impressive franchise record vs. Celtics|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=November 29, 2024|access-date=November 30, 2024}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2025–present)===
On February 3, 2025, LaVine, [[Sidy Cissoko]], three first-round draft picks and three second-round draft picks, were traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in a three-team trade also involving the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Acquire Zach Lavine, Sidy Cissoko and Multiple Draft Picks in Three-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-zach-lavine-sidy-cissoko-and-multiple-draft-picks-in-three-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2025|access-date=February 3, 2025}}</ref> On February 24, LaVine scored a season-high 42 points on 16-of-19 shooting and 8 for 9 from three-point range in a 130–88 win over the [[2024–25 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Zach LaVine scores season-high 42 points to help Kings beat Hornets 130-88|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/zach-lavine-scores-season-high-42-points-kings-119154107|website=ABC news|date=February 24, 2025|access-date=February 25, 2025}}</ref>

LaVine made 39 appearances (36 starts) for Sacramento during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], averaging 19.2 points, 2.8 rebounds and 2.3 assists. On February 13, 2026, it was announced that LaVine would require season-ending surgery to repair a tendon injury in his right hand.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kings star to undergo season-ending surgery |url=https://basketnews.com/news-241190-kings-star-to-undergo-season-ending-surgery.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=14 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Lavine was selected as one of the players on Team USA at the [[2020 Summer Olympics]] in Tokyo, Japan, which was postponed to 2021 due to the novel coronavirus [[COVID-19]] global pandemic. He started one game and played primarily as the team's sixth man, averaging 10.6 points per game. Prior to the gold medal game, he was second in assists, playing solid defense and was shooting a team-best 47% from three-point range. LaVine and Team USA won the [[Olympic gold medal]] in men's basketball.
